findings.asked: Calculate the kinetic energy of a moving object.
findings.wentWrong: A surprising number could not write the formula at all; only the most able reached 180 with the unit J.
findings.rule: KE = 1/2 m v^2 - no formula, no marks.

findings.asked: Kinetic energy, then the height a ball was dropped from using its potential energy.
findings.wentWrong: The KE parts were well answered but full of arithmetic slips, most often a mass left in grams; the height calculation used the wrong value for the potential energy.
findings.rule: Mass in kg, then GPE = mgh with the energy value the question actually gives.

findings.asked: Kinetic energy at the bottom of a fall when the object already had 10 J at the top, to one decimal place.
findings.wentWrong: 100 J was found, but a large number forgot to add the initial 10 J (or subtracted it), and a significant minority ignored the one-decimal-place instruction.
findings.rule: Total energy at the bottom = energy at the top + energy gained; then obey the rounding instruction.

findings.asked: Maximum height of a golf ball from its energy, then its speed on hitting the ground.
findings.wentWrong: A significant minority left g out of the potential-energy formula; for the speed, the total energy at the top was not carried into the kinetic-energy step, so the wrong value was used.
findings.rule: GPE = m x g x h with g = 10 N/kg; energy is conserved, so use the total.

ruleToRemember: KE = 1/2 m v^2 and GPE = m g h, with mass in kg, speed in m/s and g = 10 N/kg. Write the equation, convert units, substitute, answer with J. Energy is conserved: KE gained = GPE lost, plus whatever energy the object started with.
aStarSignal: Chaining GPE to KE to speed (or height) in one clean line with the initial energy included and the answer rounded as instructed.
